stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \ln\left| x - 1 \right| + \frac{\left(x^{2} - 25\right)\left(x^{2} - x - 2\right)}{\left(x^{2} + 3 x - 10\right)\left(x + 1\right)} \). The graph of \( f \) has exactly one vertical asymptote, the line \( x = c \). Find the value of \( c \).

worked_solution.text: The rational part has numerator \( \left(x - 5\right) \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 5\right) \) and denominator \( \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 5\right) \).

The factors at \( x = -5 \), \( x = -1 \), and \( x = 2 \) divide out, so away from those inputs the rational part equals \( x - 5 \), a polynomial. Those three inputs are removable discontinuities, not asymptotes.
The only input left where \( f \) is undefined is \( x = 1 \), where \( \ln\left| x - 1 \right| \) is undefined.
As \( x \to 1 \) from either side, \( \left| x - 1 \right| \to 0^+ \), so the logarithm decreases without bound while the polynomial part stays finite: \( f(x) \to -\infty \) on both sides.
So the line \( x = 1 \) is the only vertical asymptote, and \( c = 1 \).
